title: Practice Set STS3 — Exactly-Once Across Team Boundaries
description: Senior streaming recognition track. Module 3 of 5 — exactly-once across team boundaries.

datasets.description: Schema reference (sample rows). Senior scenarios describe GridUnion Continental at platform scale (8M+ meters, 6 teams, 4 countries, 30 regions); the CSV is a small sample for schema reference.

tasks.title: Exactly-Once Across a Team Boundary

description.context: Exactly-once semantics across a TEAM BOUNDARY is a different problem than exactly-once within a single query. Team Anomaly's streaming query writes anomaly events to a downstream Kafka topic 'team.anomaly.events' which Team Regulatory consumes for compliance reports. Team Anomaly's query has perfect exactly-once internally (Delta sink, checkpoint, idempotent writes). But if Team Anomaly's query restarts and replays a batch that was already written to the downstream Kafka topic, Team Regulatory sees duplicates UNLESS the producer write to Kafka is configured for transactional exactly-once. Cross-team exactly-once requires the SINK BOUNDARY to be transactional. Kafka producer transactional configuration (transactional.id, idempotence.enable, isolation.level=read_committed on consumer side) is the contract that makes cross-team exactly-once work.
description.task: Why does this cross-team configuration achieve exactly-once, and what would break it?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Producer Team: Team Anomaly — writes to topic 'team.anomaly.events'

Consumer Team: Team Regulatory — reads from topic for compliance reporting

Team Anomaly Internal: exactly-once within their query (Delta sink, checkpoint)

Concern: after Team Anomaly's query restarts, Team Regulatory may see duplicates

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: GridUnion Team Anomaly's pipeline writes to downstream Kafka; Team Regulatory's pipeline reads from it; what configuration spans the boundary

evidence.label: Plan output
evidence.content:
# Team Anomaly's producer pipeline
q_anomaly = (anomalies.writeStream
    .format('kafka')
    .option('kafka.bootstrap.servers', 'kafka:9092')
    .option('topic', 'team.anomaly.events')
    .option('kafka.transactional.id', 'team-anomaly-producer')   # ← transactional ID set
    .option('kafka.enable.idempotence', 'true')                  # ← idempotent producer
    .option('checkpointLocation', 's3://anomaly/ckpt')
    .start())

# Team Regulatory's consumer pipeline
q_regulatory = (spark.readStream.format('kafka')
    .option('subscribe', 'team.anomaly.events')
    .option('kafka.isolation.level', 'read_committed')           # ← reads committed only
    .load()
    ...)

# Cross-team contract:
#   Team Anomaly: transactional producer with stable transactional.id
#   Team Regulatory: read_committed consumer
# Together: Team Regulatory sees only fully-committed batches; uncommitted/aborted writes invisible.
#
# What happens on Team Anomaly's restart mid-batch:
#   1. Crashed batch's transaction is ABORTED on broker recovery
#   2. Replayed batch writes a fresh transaction with the same data
#   3. Team Regulatory's read_committed consumer sees only the committed (replayed) transaction

fields.label: Why does this cross-team configuration achieve exactly-once, and what would break it?
options: Spark's checkpoint location alone provides cross-team exactly-once; Kafka transactional configuration is redundant safety. The contract works because Team Anomaly's checkpoint replays the same offsets, and Kafka topics are inherently exactly-once.

Spark's checkpoint location alone provides cross-team exactly-once; the Kafka transactional configuration is redundant safety. The contract works because Team Anomaly's checkpoint replays the exact same offsets, and Kafka topics are inherently exactly-once.

The configuration achieves at-most-once, not exactly-once. Cross-team exactly-once is impossible in Kafka because consumers cannot coordinate with producer transactions across cluster boundaries reliably. Team Regulatory must implement application-level deduplication.

Cross-team exactly-once requires three coordinated configs: producer transactional.id stable across restarts, producer idempotence to deduplicate retries, and consumer read_committed isolation to filter uncommitted writes. Removing any one breaks the contract.
fields.correctAnswer: Cross-team exactly-once requires three coordinated configs: producer transactional.id stable across restarts, producer idempotence to deduplicate retries, and consumer read_committed isolation to filter uncommitted writes. Removing any one breaks the contract.
fields.rationale: Cross-team exactly-once via Kafka requires three coordinated pieces.
fields.distractorRationale: id; only producers have transactional IDs.

tasks.title: Cross-Team Contract Drift Caused Duplicates

description.context: Cross-team contracts drift when one team makes a unilateral change. Team Regulatory's compliance reports show duplicate anomaly events. Investigation reveals: Team Anomaly's pipeline still has transactional.id and enable.idempotence configured. Team Regulatory's consumer recently changed isolation.level from 'read_committed' back to default 'read_uncommitted' as part of a config migration — without realizing that this default reads in-flight writes including those from aborted transactions. The cost-asymmetry calculus is brutal: Team Regulatory's change took 2 minutes (just an option removed); Team Anomaly's pipeline produces ~1,000 anomaly events per second with ~0.1% restart-related transaction aborts; the duplicate rate is now 1 event per second visible to compliance reports. Every restart of Team Anomaly's pipeline now contaminates Team Regulatory's regulatory submission for that period.
description.task: Why did this 2-minute config change cause 3,600 duplicates per hour, and what is the broader Senior lesson?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Incident: compliance reports show ~3,600 duplicate anomaly events per hour after a 2-minute config change at Team Regulatory

Team Anomaly Config: transactional.id='team-anomaly-producer', enable.idempotence=true (unchanged for 6 months)

Team Regulatory Change: removed 'kafka.isolation.level' option from consumer config 3 days ago

Team Regulatory Explanation In Pr: removed unused option to clean up config

Team Anomaly Restarts Per Day: ~12 (cluster autoscaling, occasional spot reclaim)

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: GridUnion incident — Team Regulatory's read_committed isolation removed; duplicates appear in compliance reports

evidence.label: Plan output
evidence.content:
# Team Regulatory's consumer pipeline — BEFORE the config migration
q = (spark.readStream.format('kafka')
        .option('subscribe', 'team.anomaly.events')
        .option('kafka.isolation.level', 'read_committed')   # ← previously here
        ...)

# Team Regulatory's consumer pipeline — AFTER the config migration
q = (spark.readStream.format('kafka')
        .option('subscribe', 'team.anomaly.events')
        # kafka.isolation.level removed — defaults to 'read_uncommitted'
        ...)

# Compliance report duplicate count
# Day -7 (before change):    avg 3 duplicate events / hour (random network noise)
# Day +1 (after change):     1,400 duplicates / hour
# Day +3 (current):          3,600 duplicates / hour (more autoscaling events accumulating)
#
# Team Regulatory PR description:
#   'Removed unused kafka.isolation.level option for cleanliness; default is fine.'
# Reviewer (also Team Regulatory): 'LGTM, ship it.'

fields.label: Why did this 2-minute config change cause 3,600 duplicates per hour, and what is the broader Senior lesson?
options: The duplicates are unrelated to isolation.level; they are caused by Kafka topic compaction lag at the broker level. The 3-day timing coincides with topic compaction starting to fall behind on the cluster. Fix: increase topic compaction frequency.

The duplicates are unrelated to isolation.level; they are caused by Kafka topic compaction lag. The 3-day timing coincides with topic compaction starting to fall behind. Fix: increase topic compaction frequency.
Spark Structured Streaming's read_committed support has a known bug in 3.5; the change exposed that bug. Fix: upgrade to Spark 3.5.1 which patches the issue. The PR change was correct in principle.

Removing read_committed reverts to read_uncommitted (Kafka default), exposing aborted producer transactions. Senior lesson: cross-team config is a CONTRACT requiring cross-team review — neither side changes unilaterally.
fields.correctAnswer: Removing read_committed reverts to read_uncommitted (Kafka default), exposing aborted producer transactions. Senior lesson: cross-team config is a CONTRACT requiring cross-team review — neither side changes unilaterally.
fields.rationale: Kafka's default consumer isolation is read_uncommitted — the consumer sees ALL writes including those from in-flight or aborted transactions.
fields.distractorRationale: Option A: Blames producer config; the producer is correctly configured.
